Local search (best known so far)

A min-conflicts local search over the cover condition improves on the RL rows.
Every set below was verified to cover all nonzero residues modulo `N`. The
method is incomplete: these are the best sets found, not proven optima. The
bound `d(d-1)+1 >= N` gives `d >= 13` for `N <= 157`, `d >= 14` for
`158 <= N <= 183`, and `d >= 15` for `184 <= N <= 211`, so most rows are within
one or two of it.

The table runs from `N = 151` to `241` without gaps, and nothing was found above
`241`. `N = 183` is the Singer optimum of the table above (`d = 14`), so the
local search resumes at `184`, where `d = 15` is the open target and the listed
set uses one more element. From `N = 196` the table uses 17 elements, except
where a 17-element set was not found and 18 are used instead: `219`, and
everything from `221` up. Neither `d = 15` nor `d = 16` is proved impossible
anywhere in this range.

For `N = 176` to `182`, `d = 14` is proved impossible: by parity counting for
`182`, and by completed exhaustive searches (`diff_cover`, fifteen threads) for
`176` to `181`. The next target there is `d = 15`, so the 16-element sets listed
below are not known to be optimal.

`N = 196` and above use 17 elements because no 16-element set was found there:
nine seed families of search at `196` and `197` (about 7.5 h and 5.5 h of
ten-thread work) and five at `198` and `199` all came back empty. That is a
limit of this local search, not a proof that 15 or 16 elements are impossible in
that range.

Four devices make the upper range reachable at all. A **greedy start** builds
each initial set by maximising newly covered classes instead of picking
uniformly. **Warm starts** come from a cover one element larger, whose extra
element is dropped at each restart. An **antipodal move** handles the class
`N/2`, which only a pair `(t, t + N/2)` can cover and the plain same-element
move cannot create. A **tabu list** on values, with aspiration, stops the search
oscillating between two states that each miss one class.

`N = 218` and `220` needed 81 and 24 minutes respectively, the former only after
the warm start. They are islands rather than a frontier: `N = 219` resisted two
hours of cold search and seven 30-minute warm repairs at `d = 17`, and `221` and
`222` each took an hour of cold search plus four warm repairs, all without a
result. At this density the method either lands on a cover or stalls one or two
classes short, and which of the two happens is decided by the seed, not by the
budget. One more element removes the difficulty entirely: with `d = 18` all
three fall in seconds to minutes (`219` in 2 s, `221` in 24 s, `222` in 2 s).

The `d = 18` block is complete through `241`. Getting there needed the long
horizon on the last five interior gaps: `234` in 10 min, `235` in 57 min, `236`
in 11 min, `238` in 51 min and `240` in 17 min, all from a cold greedy start
without any warm-start help. Beyond `241` the spare capacity runs out again:
`242` to `245` produced nothing, and at `N = 256` the search stalls 12 classes
short, with 153 pairs for 128 classes.
